## One Program, Two Emissions Rules

The program used different rules for sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. Its sulfur dioxide mechanism applied an aggregate cap and allowed allowance trading, with each allowance covering one ton. The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units; it began in 1996 and did not introduce a cap or allowance trading.

Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap for 2010 was 8.95 million tons.
